answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cost reduction; the incumbent has closed the door on price this cycle, so negotiation with them (memory_c1, memory_c6) is dead-ended for this objective. Memory_c2 records that a prior switch to the low-cost vendor delivered a sharp unit-cost cut with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing — directly relevant to whether a switch can be executed inside the 14-day window without introducing delivery risk. Memory_c4 records that benchmarking against market rates moved the incumbent on price and terms at renewal; if the incumbent is truly immovable, that path is closed, but verifying it confirms whether a competitive quote could still be used as leverage rather than a full switch. The assembly line is at 94% with no buffer, so delivery continuity is the binding constraint; c2's record of clean onboarding and c4's record of successful benchmarking together give the strongest basis for a controlled switch. Deferring (c5) is not viable because the contract does not auto-renew. Adding a second source (c3) addresses concentration risk but does not by itself deliver the 18% cut. With one decision slot, switching primary supply to the lower-cost vendor is the only direction that meets both the cost mandate and, per the verified record, the delivery-risk constraint.
